title: Futur I and Futur II
description: Expressing assumptions about the present (Futur I) and assumptions about the past (Futur II).

examples.german: Er wird wohl im Stau stehen.
examples.english: He is probably stuck in traffic (Futur I - Assumption).

examples.german: Sie wird den Zug verpasst haben.
examples.english: She probably missed the train (Futur II).

conjugationTable: Futur II: werden + Past Participle + haben/sein
Ich werde gegessen haben (I will have eaten)
errorTraps: In B2, Futur tenses are rarely used to talk about the future! We use Present tense for the future. We use Futur I & II to express ASSUMPTIONS.

title: Partizipialattribute
description: Turning entire sentences into massive adjectives that stand in front of a noun.

examples.german: Der auf dem Tisch liegende Stift ist blau.
examples.english: The pen lying on the table is blue.

examples.german: Das von Picasso gemalte Bild ist teuer.
examples.english: The picture painted by Picasso is expensive.

conjugationTable: Partizip I (Active): Infinitive + d + Adjective Ending (spielend-)
Partizip II (Passive): Past Participle + Adjective Ending (gekauft-)
errorTraps: All the extra information MUST go between the article and the participle! (Der [in Berlin wohnende] Mann).

title: Konjunktiv I (Indirect Speech)
description: How to report what someone else said without guaranteeing it's true.

examples.german: Er sagt, er habe keine Zeit.
examples.english: He says he has no time.

examples.german: Der Politiker behauptet, er sei unschuldig.
examples.english: The politician claims he is innocent.

conjugationTable: sein: ich sei, du seiest, er sei, wir seien, ihr seiet, sie seien
haben: ich habe, du habest, er habe...
For regular verbs, drop the 'n' from the infinitive: er gehe, sie mache
errorTraps: Only the 3rd person singular (er/sie/es) looks clearly different in Konjunktiv I. For 'ich' and 'wir', it looks like normal present tense, so Germans switch to Konjunktiv II to make it clear it's indirect speech!

title: Passive Alternatives
description: Ways to express a passive meaning without actually using 'werden'.
errorTraps: Remember that 'sein + zu' implies a NECESSITY (muss) in official language, but a POSSIBILITY (kann) in scientific language.

title: Nomen-Verb-Verbindungen
description: Formal noun-verb combinations that replace simple verbs in business and politics.
conjugationTable: zur Verfügung stehen - to be available
einen Antrag stellen - to submit an application
in Anspruch nehmen - to make use of
errorTraps: Do not translate literally! 'To MAKE a decision' is 'eine Entscheidung TREFFEN' (hit a decision), not 'machen'.
